title: Board-pattern readiness test — most-repeated question types
chapter: CBSE Class 12 Geography (029) · both books and both map units, weighted by the 2026-27 theory marks
tagline: Practice questions modelled on past CBSE papers; not predictions of this year's paper.
disclaimer: Original questions written for Teraminds Academy from the NCERT textbooks prescribed for 2026-27, modelled on the most-repeated question types in CBSE board papers 2023–26 and the Sample Question Paper 2026-27 (see our Board Blueprint). A board-pattern readiness test for practice only: not a prediction of any exam and no promise of marks.
instructions: 36 questions. MCQ and assertion-reason: choose one option. Numeric: type a whole number (no units).

A1.name: A-1 · Human Geography: Nature and Scope (3 marks)
A1.tip: Early humans adapted to nature: 'naturalisation of humans' = environmental determinism. Humans then shaped nature: possibilism ('humanisation of nature'). Griffith Taylor's middle path: neo-determinism, 'stop and go' determinism.
A1.ncert: NCERT Fundamentals of Human Geography (Class 12, 2026-27): Ch 1 Human Geography

A2.name: A-2 · World Population; Human Development (8 marks)
A2.tip: Natural growth = birth rate − death rate. Demographic transition: stage 1 high birth and death rates, stage 3 both low. Human development (Mahbub-ul-Haq, 1990): four pillars equity, sustainability, productivity, empowerment.
A2.ncert: NCERT Fundamentals of Human Geography (Class 12, 2026-27): Ch 2 The World Population, Ch 3 Human Development

A3.name: A-3 · Primary, Secondary, Tertiary & Quaternary Activities; Transport, Communication & Trade (19 marks)
A3.tip: Commercial livestock rearing = ranches, one animal type, scientific. Plantations: Europeans in colonies, one crop, large estates. Footloose industries: not tied to raw materials, component-based, low polluting. Quinary = top decision makers. Trans-Siberian: St Petersburg–Vladivostok. Suez (1869) joins Mediterranean and Red Sea. Negative balance of trade = imports > exports. Entrepot ports re-export (Singapore, Rotterdam). WTO 1995.
A3.ncert: NCERT Fundamentals of Human Geography (Class 12, 2026-27): Ch 4 Primary Activities, Ch 5 Secondary Activities, Ch 6 Tertiary and Quaternary Activities, Ch 7 Transport and Communication, Ch 8 International Trade

AM.name: A-Map · World political map (5 marks)
AM.tip: Learn the curriculum's world map list: areas of farming (e.g. Prairies), major seaports, canals (Suez, Panama with their terminal ports), transcontinental railway terminals.
AM.ncert: CBSE Geography curriculum 2026-27: world map list (with Fundamentals Ch 4, 7, 8)

B1.name: B-I · India: Population (5 marks)
B1.tip: Census 2011: Bihar has the highest density, Arunachal Pradesh the lowest. Growth phases: 1901–21 stagnant, 1921–51 steady (falling death rate), 1951–81 population explosion, after 1981 the growth rate slows.
B1.ncert: NCERT India: People and Economy (Class 12, 2026-27): Ch 1 Population: Distribution, Density, Growth and Composition

B2.name: B-II · India: Human Settlements (3 marks)
B2.tip: Rural types: clustered, semi-clustered, hamleted (panna, para, palli, nagla, dhani), dispersed. Towns by function: administrative, industrial, transport, commercial, mining (Raniganj, Jharia, Digboi), garrison (Ambala, Jalandhar, Mhow), religious, educational.
B2.ncert: NCERT India: People and Economy (Class 12, 2026-27): Ch 2 Human Settlements

B3.name: B-III · Land, Agriculture, Water, Minerals & Energy, Planning (10 marks)
B3.tip: Current fallow = left uncultivated for one year or less. Watershed programmes: Haryali, Neeru-Meeru (Andhra Pradesh), Arvary Pani Sansad (Alwar, Rajasthan). Bharmaur: Gaddi tribe, Himachal Pradesh. Indira Gandhi Canal starts at the Harike barrage; sustainability needs water discipline and shelter belts.
B3.ncert: NCERT India: People and Economy (Class 12, 2026-27): Ch 3 Land Resources and Agriculture, Ch 4 Water Resources, Ch 5 Mineral and Energy Resources, Ch 6 Planning and Sustainable Development in Indian Context

B4.name: B-IV · India: Transport, Communication and Trade (7 marks)
B4.tip: Golden Quadrilateral: Delhi–Mumbai–Chennai–Kolkata. Konkan Railway (1998): Roha (Maharashtra) to Mangaluru (Karnataka). HBJ gas pipeline: Hazira–Bijaipur–Jagdishpur. Kandla was built after Partition to ease Mumbai's load after the loss of Karachi.
B4.ncert: NCERT India: People and Economy (Class 12, 2026-27): Ch 7 Transport and Communication, Ch 8 International Trade

B5.name: B-V · Geographical Perspective on Selected Issues (5 marks)
B5.tip: Pollution types and sources; noise is measured in decibels. Dharavi (Mumbai) as a case of slums. Human-made land degradation: waterlogging, salinity and alkalinity from over-irrigation; mining, deforestation.
B5.ncert: NCERT India: People and Economy (Class 12, 2026-27): Ch 9 Geographical Perspective on Selected Issues and Problems

BM.name: B-Map · India political map (5 marks)
BM.tip: Learn the curriculum's India map list: leading crop states, iron-ore/manganese/copper/bauxite/coal mines, refineries (Mathura, Jamnagar, Barauni), 10 seaports and 10 international airports.
BM.ncert: CBSE Geography curriculum 2026-27: India map list (with India: People and Economy Ch 3, 5, 7, 8)

questions.question: The idea of neo-determinism ('stop and go' determinism) was put forward by:
questions.explanation: Taylor proposed a middle path between environmental determinism and possibilism.
questions.remediation: A-1 · Human Geography: Nature and Scope (3 marks): NCERT Fundamentals of Human Geography (Class 12, 2026-27): Ch 1 Human Geography; then the question types listed for this unit in the Blueprint PDF.

questions.question: In early human societies, people were heavily dependent on nature and adapted to it. Human geographers call this stage the 'naturalisation of humans', which corresponds to:
questions.explanation: With primitive technology, nature dictated human life: environmental determinism. Possibilism = 'humanisation of nature'.
questions.remediation: A-1 · Human Geography: Nature and Scope (3 marks): NCERT Fundamentals of Human Geography (Class 12, 2026-27): Ch 1 Human Geography; then the question types listed for this unit in the Blueprint PDF.

questions.question: The concept of human development was introduced by:
questions.explanation: Dr Mahbub-ul-Haq; the UNDP has published the Human Development Report since 1990.
questions.remediation: A-2 · World Population; Human Development (8 marks): NCERT Fundamentals of Human Geography (Class 12, 2026-27): Ch 2 The World Population, Ch 3 Human Development; then the question types listed for this unit in the Blueprint PDF.

questions.question: Which of these is NOT one of the four pillars of human development?
questions.explanation: The four pillars: equity, sustainability, productivity and empowerment.
questions.remediation: A-2 · World Population; Human Development (8 marks): NCERT Fundamentals of Human Geography (Class 12, 2026-27): Ch 2 The World Population, Ch 3 Human Development; then the question types listed for this unit in the Blueprint PDF.

questions.question: In the first stage of the demographic transition theory:
questions.explanation: Stage 1: high and fluctuating birth and death rates, slow growth; stage 3: both low.
questions.remediation: A-2 · World Population; Human Development (8 marks): NCERT Fundamentals of Human Geography (Class 12, 2026-27): Ch 2 The World Population, Ch 3 Human Development; then the question types listed for this unit in the Blueprint PDF.
options: Both fertility and mortality are high
Fertility is high and mortality falls sharply
Both fertility and mortality are low

questions.question: A town of 50,000 people has a crude birth rate of 30 and a crude death rate of 10 (per thousand per year). Ignoring migration, by how many people does its population grow in a year?
questions.explanation: Natural growth rate = 30 − 10 = 20 per thousand; 20/1000 × 50,000 = 1,000.
questions.remediation: A-2 · World Population; Human Development (8 marks): NCERT Fundamentals of Human Geography (Class 12, 2026-27): Ch 2 The World Population, Ch 3 Human Development; then the question types listed for this unit in the Blueprint PDF.

questions.question: The Trans-Siberian Railway connects:
questions.explanation: It is Asia's longest double-tracked, electrified transcontinental railway.
questions.remediation: A-3 · Primary, Secondary, Tertiary & Quaternary Activities; Transport, Communication & Trade (19 marks): NCERT Fundamentals of Human Geography (Class 12, 2026-27): Ch 4 Primary Activities, Ch 5 Secondary Activities, Ch 6 Tertiary and Quaternary Activities, Ch 7 Transport and Communication, Ch 8 International Trade; then the question types listed for this unit in the Blueprint PDF.
options: St Petersburg in the west with Vladivostok in the east

questions.question: The Suez Canal links:
questions.explanation: Opened in 1869, it shortened the route between Europe and Asia; Panama links the Atlantic and Pacific.
questions.remediation: A-3 · Primary, Secondary, Tertiary & Quaternary Activities; Transport, Communication & Trade (19 marks): NCERT Fundamentals of Human Geography (Class 12, 2026-27): Ch 4 Primary Activities, Ch 5 Secondary Activities, Ch 6 Tertiary and Quaternary Activities, Ch 7 Transport and Communication, Ch 8 International Trade; then the question types listed for this unit in the Blueprint PDF.
options: The Black Sea and the Caspian Sea
The Baltic Sea and the North Sea
The Mediterranean Sea and the Red Sea

questions.question: Commercial livestock rearing differs from nomadic herding because it:
questions.explanation: Ranching is capital-intensive, scientific and market-oriented.
questions.remediation: A-3 · Primary, Secondary, Tertiary & Quaternary Activities; Transport, Communication & Trade (19 marks): NCERT Fundamentals of Human Geography (Class 12, 2026-27): Ch 4 Primary Activities, Ch 5 Secondary Activities, Ch 6 Tertiary and Quaternary Activities, Ch 7 Transport and Communication, Ch 8 International Trade; then the question types listed for this unit in the Blueprint PDF.
options: Is organised on permanent ranches, specialises in one type of animal and uses scientific methods
Moves with animals from place to place for pasture

questions.question: Plantation agriculture was introduced in many tropical countries by:
questions.explanation: Large estates growing a single crop (tea, coffee, rubber, sugarcane) with capital and cheap labour.
questions.remediation: A-3 · Primary, Secondary, Tertiary & Quaternary Activities; Transport, Communication & Trade (19 marks): NCERT Fundamentals of Human Geography (Class 12, 2026-27): Ch 4 Primary Activities, Ch 5 Secondary Activities, Ch 6 Tertiary and Quaternary Activities, Ch 7 Transport and Communication, Ch 8 International Trade; then the question types listed for this unit in the Blueprint PDF.

questions.question: Footloose industries are those that:
questions.explanation: They use component parts, employ small labour forces and are usually non-polluting.
questions.remediation: A-3 · Primary, Secondary, Tertiary & Quaternary Activities; Transport, Communication & Trade (19 marks): NCERT Fundamentals of Human Geography (Class 12, 2026-27): Ch 4 Primary Activities, Ch 5 Secondary Activities, Ch 6 Tertiary and Quaternary Activities, Ch 7 Transport and Communication, Ch 8 International Trade; then the question types listed for this unit in the Blueprint PDF.
options: Depend entirely on agricultural raw materials
Must be located near coal fields
Can be located in a wide variety of places because they are not tied to a specific raw material

questions.question: Quinary activities involve:
questions.explanation: Quinary is the highest level of decision making and policy formulation.
questions.remediation: A-3 · Primary, Secondary, Tertiary & Quaternary Activities; Transport, Communication & Trade (19 marks): NCERT Fundamentals of Human Geography (Class 12, 2026-27): Ch 4 Primary Activities, Ch 5 Secondary Activities, Ch 6 Tertiary and Quaternary Activities, Ch 7 Transport and Communication, Ch 8 International Trade; then the question types listed for this unit in the Blueprint PDF.
options: Senior business executives, government officials and decision makers ('gold collar')

questions.question: A country has a negative balance of trade when:
questions.explanation: A negative (unfavourable) balance means spending more on imports than earning from exports.

options: The value of its imports exceeds the value of its exports

questions.question: Singapore and Rotterdam act as collection centres where goods are brought from many countries for re-export. Such ports are called:
questions.explanation: Entrepot = collection and re-export; packet stations carry passengers and mail over short distances.
questions.remediation: A-3 · Primary, Secondary, Tertiary & Quaternary Activities; Transport, Communication & Trade (19 marks): NCERT Fundamentals of Human Geography (Class 12, 2026-27): Ch 4 Primary Activities, Ch 5 Secondary Activities, Ch 6 Tertiary and Quaternary Activities, Ch 7 Transport and Communication, Ch 8 International Trade; then the question types listed for this unit in the Blueprint PDF.

questions.remediation: A-3 · Primary, Secondary, Tertiary & Quaternary Activities; Transport, Communication & Trade (19 marks): NCERT Fundamentals of Human Geography (Class 12, 2026-27): Ch 4 Primary Activities, Ch 5 Secondary Activities, Ch 6 Tertiary and Quaternary Activities, Ch 7 Transport and Communication, Ch 8 International Trade; then the question types listed for this unit in the Blueprint PDF.

questions.question: Which measure would best promote ecological sustainability in the Indira Gandhi Canal command area?

Letting water flow freely without any rotation
Strict water management and planting shelter belts, with less area under water-intensive crops
Expanding rice cultivation everywhere along the canal
